status.nb: 4 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 56 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Caracas, Valencia og Maracaibo.

summary.en: Venezuela disclosed a $237.5 billion debt pile and is moving toward a large restructuring while the United States signed a military cooperation pact with the interim Venezuelan government, after which a U.S. marine died falling overboard during a Caribbean operation linked to the renewed ties. Senate investigations target JD Vance for allegedly steering a Venezuelan oil license to Vitol and a separate probe examines another senator’s role in the same deal, while Citi considers re-entering the market after a five-year exit and the pact was later declared null and void by Venezuelan authorities. Illegal gold mining continues, and Eni and Repsol pledged $2 billion in joint-venture investments. According to UCDP, there were 2 battle-related deaths in 2007.
summary.nb: Venezuela offentliggjorde en gjeld på $237.5 milliarder og går mot en omfattende restrukturering, mens USA signerte en militær samarbeidsavtale med den midlertidige venezuelanske regjeringen, hvoretter en amerikansk marine døde etter å ha falt overbord under en karibisk operasjon knyttet til de fornyede båndene. Senatets etterforskninger retter seg mot JD Vance for angivelig å ha styrt en venezuelansk oljelisens til Vitol, og en separat etterforskning undersøker en annen senators rolle i samme avtale, mens Citi vurderer å gå inn i markedet igjen etter en femårsavgang, og avtalen ble senere erklært ugyldig av venezuelanske myndigheter. Ulovlig gullgruvedrift fortsetter, og Eni og Repsol lovet 2 milliarder dollar i joint-venture-investeringer. Ifølge UCDP var det 2 dødsfall i kamp i 2007.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro as well as Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
